## strings and regex

```{r}
string_vec = c("my", "name", "is", "meghan")

str_detect(string_vec, "meghan")
str_replace(string_vec, "meghan", "Meghan")
```

* `str_detect`: detects patterns of character vectors (words, letters, number) that is either true or false. CASE SENSITIVE!
* so meghan is true 1 out of the 4 vectors, m is true 3 out of 4, etc. 
* `str_replace`: replaces character vector with whatever character word/letter/number

```{r}
string_vec = c(
  "i think we all rule for participating",
  "i think i have been caught",
  "i think this will be quite fun actually",
  "it will be fun, i think"
  )

str_detect(string_vec, "^i think")
str_detect(string_vec, "i think$")
```

* `^` at the beginning of the phrase line, so vectors that start with "i think"
* `$` at the end of the phrase line, so vectors that ends with "i think"

```{r}
string_vec = c(
  "Time for a Pumpkin Spice Latte!",
  "went to the #pumpkinpatch last weekend",
  "Pumpkin Pie is obviously the best pie",
  "SMASHING PUMPKINS -- LIVE IN CONCERT!!"
  )

str_detect(string_vec,"[Pp]umpkin")
```

* `[]` grabs lower- and uppercase...NOT case sensitive!

```{r}
string_vec = c(
  '7th inning stretch',
  '1st half soon to begin. Texas won the toss.',
  'she is 5 feet 4 inches tall',
  '3AM - cant sleep :('
  )

str_detect(string_vec, "^[0-9][a-zA-Z]")
```

* number first, followed by a letter after (ex. rankings)

```{r}
string_vec = c(
  'Its 7:11 in the evening',
  'want to go to 7-11?',
  'my flight is AA711',
  'NetBios: scanning ip 203.167.114.66'
  )

str_detect(string_vec, "7.11")
str_detect(string_vec, "7\\.11")
```

* adding a `.` is a special character that captures a character between the specified number/letter
* `\\` is a special character and it gets the exact character, no other combinations

```{r}
string_vec = c(
  'The CI is [2, 5]',
  ':-]',
  ':-[',
  'I found the answer on pages [6-7]'
  )

str_detect(string_vec, "\\[")
```

## factors

```{r}
factor_vec = factor(c("male", "male", "female", "female"))

as.numeric(factor_vec)
```

* `as.numeric`: converts character vector into values

what happens if i relevel?

```{r}
factor_vec = fct_relevel(factor_vec, "male")

as.numeric(factor_vec)
```

* `fct_relevel`: reassigns factor character to a position...before, values are automatically are ordered alphabetically

## NSDUH -- strings

```{r}
url = "https://www.samhsa.gov/data/sites/default/files/NSDUHsaeShortTermCHG2015/NSDUHsaeShortTermCHG2015.htm"

table_mj =
  read_html(url) |> 
  html_table() |> 
  first() |> 
  slice(-1)
```

```{r}
data_mj =
  table_mj |> 
  select(-contains("P Value")) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    -State,
    names_to = "age_year",
    values_to = "percent"
  ) |> 
  separate(age_year, into = c("age","year"), sep = "\\(") |> 
  mutate(
    year = str_replace(year, "\\)", ""),
    percent = str_replace(percent, "[a-c]$",""),
    percent = as.numeric(percent)
  ) |> 
  filter(!(State %in% c("Total U.S.", "Northeast", "Midwest", "South", "West")))
```

* `contains` similar to `str_detect`
* the dash (`-`) indicates a removal (no dash means inclusion)
* `sep = `similar to `str_detect`, but for `separate` function
* `!`: don't want it, filter it out
* `%in%`: selecting which characters to filter

## NSDUH -- factors

```{r}
data_mj |> 
  filter(age == "12-17") |> 
  mutate(State = fct_reorder(State, percent)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = State, y = percent, color = year)) +
  geom_point() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1))
```

* `fct_reorder`: orders one character (State) based on another character (percent) and takes the median value of character 1; it ranks lowest to highest
